ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a bicyclic skeleton in which a benzene ring is fused with a saturated six-membered ring; at the upper-right position of the saturated ring there is a carbonyl C=O, on the right side there is an ammonia molecule labeled :NH3, and a curved arrow is drawn from near the ammonia toward the carbonyl carbon; a carbon below the saturated ring is connected to a sulfur/nitrogen-containing substituent in the form O-SO2-NH4. The question requires ignoring arrows, so the curved arrow is not taken as bonding information, and :NH3 is treated as an ammonia fragment disconnected from the main molecule. Then reason: according to the specified transcription, the independent ammonia fragment is written as N. The fused benzo-saturated ring ketone skeleton can be encoded as C1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21, where C(=O) represents the ketone carbonyl on the saturated ring, and c2ccccc2 represents the fused benzene ring. On the lower saturated ring carbon, the substituent is connected through oxygen to the sulfate/amino oxysulfur substituent, and according to the specified chain it is converted to N-O-S(=O)-O-C, that is, NOS(=O)O is attached before that ring carbon, forming NOS(=O)OC1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21. Connect the disconnected ammonia component with a dot to obtain N.NOS(=O)OC1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First visually transcribe the molecule while explicitly deleting the curved arrows. Treat the :NH3 label as an independent ammonia fragment, giving one SMILES component N. Then trace the fused bicyclic ketone: encode the saturated ring bearing the carbonyl and fused benzene as C1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21. At the lower saturated ring carbon, attach the sulfamate/sulfate substituent through oxygen, using the drawn chain N–O–S(=O)–O–C as NOS(=O)O attached to that ring carbon. Join the disconnected ammonia component with a dot, yielding N.NOS(=O)OC1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中左侧是一个苯环与饱和六元环稠合的双环骨架，饱和环右上位置有一个羰基 C=O，右侧有一个标注为 :NH3 的氨分子，并画有从氨附近指向羰基碳的弯箭头；饱和环下方的一个碳连着 O-SO2-NH4 形式的含硫/含氮取代基。题目要求忽略箭头，因此弯箭头不作为成键信息，:NH3 作为与主分子断开的氨片段。再推理：按指定转录，独立氨片段写作 N。稠合苯并饱和环酮骨架可编码为 C1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21，其中 C(=O) 表示饱和环上的酮羰基，c2ccccc2 表示稠合苯环。在下方饱和环碳上通过氧连接硫酸/氨基氧硫取代基，按指定链转成 N-O-S(=O)-O-C，即 NOS(=O)O 接到该环碳前，形成 NOS(=O)OC1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21。将断开的氨组件用点号连接，得到 N.NOS(=O)OC1CC(=O)Cc2ccccc21。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription is the only genuinely necessary route: identify all atoms/bonds in the drawing, ignore the mechanistic arrows, and encode the disconnected fragments and fused-ring scaffold in SMILES.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as a chemical line structure: a benzene ring fused to a cyclohexanone/tetralone-like six-membered ring, with a carbonyl on the right side of the saturated ring; a substituent at the lower ring carbon drawn as O–S(=O)–O–N/H sulfamate-type group; and a separate ammonia molecule shown as :NH3 to the right. Curved arrows are present but are not part of the molecular graph.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the desired output is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: disconnected species are separated by '.', ammonia is represented as N, aromatic benzene atoms use lowercase c, carbonyl is C(=O), ring closures encode the fused bicyclic scaffold, and the drawn O–S(=O)–O–N connectivity is written as NOS(=O)O attached through O to the ring carbon. Combine the separate ammonia fragment with the substituted tetralone scaffold to obtain the final SMILES.
